analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: SIDEWAYS
key_insights: S&P 500 closed -23bps at 7,323 with a $2.1bn market-on-close imbalance to buy. NDX +42bps at 27,116, R2K +54bps at 2,716, Dow -111bps at 50,198.

NVDA finished -3% after being +2% pre-market, despite a beat/raise. Most were not surprised. GS flows in the name matched the prior night's after-hours: hedge fund buying/covering against continued long-only supply.
Hyperscalers were firm (AMZN +3%, GOOG +1%), which GS reads as rotational dynamics and a possible 'proxy' trade.

Consumer names rallied after slightly better earnings (TGT +5%, TJX +9%, LOW +70bps despite a miss). Retailers had a top-5 session YTD. Consumer has been among the most net sold sectors month to date, so GS attributes part of the move to a positioning unwind.
GS says that with the current level of uncertainty it is hard to see real sponsorship for the market.
Floor activity was 4 on a 1-10 scale. Asset manager flows were modestly muted. Hedge funds screened as small net buyers, driven by macro products. No sector currently skews materially net for sale.
ETF share of tape is 35% against a 28% YTD average.

Post-bell, PANW was +8% after hours (after +10% in the regular session). F1Q headline growth (total revenue + NGS ARR) accelerated y/y. FY RPO (y/y), operating margins and FCF margins were maintained, while the revenue and NGS ARR outlook was raised.

GS reads the Fed minutes as slightly more dovish than the headlines. On a possible 50bp move: 'A couple of participants noted that an increase of more than 25 basis points could warrant consideration at the next meeting', conditional on unfavorable incoming inflation data.

S&P traded in a spot-down, vol-down regime. GS calls this a notable and arguably more concerning shift from earlier in the week, since vol compressed after VIX expiry and NVDA earnings without equities getting a meaningful bid.
A customer bought 52.5k NVDA February call spreads into the tech weakness. Index flows were relatively subdued.
The S&P implied move through the end of the week and November regular expiry is 1.55%.
ES1 top-of-book depth averaged $4.2m at the touch, one of the worst liquidity sessions in four years, which GS says exacerbates price moves.
